text:
oncall-bot: PAGER: high CPU + KV error spike in dedicated-pool:pool-7 serving customer: Stellaris (vpc-987). Page routed to #incidents and @maria.sre. Severity: high.

maria.sre: I see the alert, picking up. Observed 5xx spike + KV read mismatch traces.

dan.engineering: Noted. Any evidence of cross-tenant reads?

maria.sre: Logs show a small set of requests hitting pool-7 with unexpected tenant-prefixes in the key. Example: `tenant:stellaris/kv:abc123` then later `tenant:partnerx/kv:abc123` in same shard. Likely prefix routing bleed in prefix-to-pool mapping.

priya.runtime: Ugh. That smells like the latebind route table update that rolled at 02:14 UTC. I have the rollout window. Could be a propagation stale map.

tess.support: Stellaris CSM pinged support - they noticed odd traces in their telemetry and asked if any cross-tenant exposure. They want a customer-facing summary ASAP.

ben.security: Priority: collect evidence, freeze state, avoid deleting logs. If there's any PII possibility treat as potential exposure until proven otherwise.

maria.sre: Agreed. Live plan: 1) Isolate pool-7 from serving new requests for Stellaris; 2) Force route re-evaluation on routing layer; 3) Capture runtime KV read logs and KV cache dump; 4) Notify SOC.

cassidy.infra: I can take isolation. Running: `rpool isolate pool-7 --reason "investigate routing bleed" --expedite` will drain external traffic and route to fallback.

priya.runtime: Before we isolate, quick check: can we do a scoped ACL enforce on tenant headers to stop ambiguous prefix matching? If quick patch exists, it might avoid full drain.

maria.sre: We need speed. Cassidy, do drain now. We'll rotate routes after we have a stable state.

cassidy.infra: Executing now. `rpool isolate` output: pool-7 transition to DRAINING -> 200/202. Redirecting new traffic to pool-9 (dedicated-reserve). ETA 45s.

oncall-bot: system: pool-7 state=draining, active connections=128 -> 18. Fallback started to pool-9.

maria.sre: Good. priya, capture current route table and the config version that rolled at 02:14. `routesv2 get --pool pool-7 --version`

priya.runtime: Copying route dump to /tmp/route-dump-pool7-2890012345.log and uploading to secure evidence bucket. Snippet: ```{ "version": "v2.7.3", "rules": [ {"prefix": "stellaris/", "pool": "pool-7"}, {"prefix": "partnerx/", "pool": "pool-7"} ] }``` Looks like two distinct tenant prefixes pointed at same pool in the same rule set. This may be intentional for consolidation but should have mutual isolation guard.

ben.security: That JSON is evidence of misconfiguration. We should flag the release that deployed v2.7.3 to change control. Who approved?

dan.engineering: That release came from runtime team with a change to prefix coalescing optimization. It aimed to reduce pools by grouping low-volume prefixes. It added a short-circuit that skipped tenant-scoped ACLs in rare cases.

maria.sre: Ok. Impact assessment: so far ~42 read ops observed with mismatched prefixes across 23 unique keys in a 7-minute window. We have no sign of consumer data read beyond key names (no payloads yet), but KV value reads were non-empty in 5 cases. We need content-level logs.

cassidy.infra: I pulled the KV read logs and uploaded; value payloads are truncated per privacy policy, but we have hashes. I'll hand to ben for further classification.

ben.security: I'll run a fast scan: compute if any hashes map to known PII markers in telemetry and if any outbound copies occurred. Also open an incident for legal contact.

priya.runtime: I'm preparing a hotfix to re-enable tenant guard and revert coalescing short-circuit: patch `runtime-routing v2.7.4` will add explicit tenant ACL check before applying coalesced rule. Test in staging now.

maria.sre: Action items and owners: Cassidy isolate (done); Priya patch + deploy to canary and pool-7 equivalent replacement (in progress); Ben evidence + security classification (in progress); Tess prepare customer note draft (drafting); Dan and I to verify logs and final impact window.

oncall-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for runtime v2.7.4 -> canary-cluster-3.

priya.runtime: Canary looks clean for 10 min, no mismatch. Ready for immediate rollback to pool route generator. Requesting deployment to edge on emergency channel.

maria.sre: Cassidy, once patch is deployed, please run `route-check --pool pool-9 --validate-tenant-guards` and then we can rehome Stellaris to pool-9 and bring pool-7 back to maintenance.

cassidy.infra: Will run checks after deployment.

ben.security: Preliminary verdict: low-probability limited exposure. No confirmed PII exfil. Recommend notifying Stellaris with transparency and offer forensic review. Legal looped in.

maria.sre: Tess, please send this to Stellaris CSM: suggested text — short, factual, what we observed, mitigation steps, timeline, and an offer for a call. Keep it conservative. I can sign off.

tess.support: Drafting now. Will post in thread for sign-off before sending.

priya.runtime: Patch deployed to edge and route generator. `runtime-routing v2.7.4` active. Running `route-check` now...

cassidy.infra: `route-check` results: tenant-guard enforced, no coalesced ambiguous rules detected on pool-9. Proceeding to migrate Stellaris traffic to pool-9.

oncall-bot: system: migration complete. pool-9 serving Stellaris. pool-7 set to MAINTENANCE.

maria.sre: Closing loop: we've isolated, patched, migrated, and captured evidence. Next: 1) ben to finish security analysis and classification, 2) dan to run a noisy-scan across other pools for similar coalescing rules, 3) priya to push release notes and a test that blocks coalescing without tenant guards, 4) cassidy to schedule a controlled audit of route tables.

ben.security: Will aim to complete initial report in 4 hours. If anything changes I'll escalate.

dan.engineering: I'll scan clusters for v2.7.3 policy and build a fix sweep script.

maria.sre: Thanks all. Summary for incident record (to paste later): timeline, root cause: routing coalescing short-circuit dropped tenant ACLs, impact: potential limited KV key cross-read (no confirmed PII), mitigation: pool isolation, patch v2.7.4, migration to pool-9, next steps and customer comms.

cassidy.infra: Leaving pool-7 in maintenance and taking an image for forensic analysis.

priya.runtime: Adding an e2e test in CI that simulates prefix collision to ensure tenant isolation is preserved.

oncall-bot: incident: status=stabilized, responders=[maria.sre, dan.engineering, priya.runtime, cassidy.infra, ben.security, tess.support].

maria.sre: I'll open the formal incident postmortem and link evidence. Good work.

tess.support: Draft shared for review — flagged for sign-off.

ben.security: Legal and SOC notified. We'll confirm customer communication content before send.

maria.sre: Thread will be archived after postmortem doc created. If anyone sees follow-up alerts, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
